name: Paradox
tagline: Classic 1985 desktop relational database with Query by Example; now a frozen extra in WordPerfect Office.
description: Paradox is a desktop relational database that Ansa Software released for MS-DOS in 1985; Borland bought Ansa in 1987 and turned it into one of the best-selling PC databases of the late 1980s and early 1990s, and Corel took it over in the mid-1990s. It paired file-based tables with a visual Query by Example interface, forms, reports and its own languages, PAL on DOS and the object-based ObjectPAL on Windows, and its table format became a common storage choice for Delphi applications through the Borland Database Engine. Corel still bundles Paradox with WordPerfect Office Professional, but the product has not seen a meaningful update since about 2009. Keep it only to maintain existing applications; move data to Access, SQLite or a server database.
statusNote: Still bundled with Corel WordPerfect Office Professional but effectively frozen since about 2009; maintain existing apps only.

pricing.notes: Available only as part of WordPerfect Office Professional.

scale.notes: File-based tables shared over a network drive; no server process.

strengths: Visual Query by Example that non-programmers can use
Forms, reports and ObjectPAL apps in one desktop package
Huge legacy of Delphi/BDE applications that read its tables
weaknesses: File-share multi-user access is fragile and prone to corruption
Only sold inside a WordPerfect Office suite
useCases: Maintaining legacy Paradox and Delphi/BDE applications
Extracting data from old .DB tables for migration
